classification.difficultyReason: Recognise both the vertical-line possibility and the tangent, parameterise a non-vertical line through the specified point, and impose a repeated intersection to derive its slope symbolically.

content.prompt: Consider the parabola defined by $y=ax^2+bx+c$. Determine the equation of the line(s) whose single point of intersection with this parabola is when $x=p$.

answer.short:
$x=p$ and $y=(2ap+b)x-ap^2+c$.

The vertical line meets the parabola once; the other line is the tangent, found by setting the discriminant to zero.
answer.worked:
The intersection point is $(p,ap^2+bp+c)$. The vertical line $x=p$ meets the parabola at this point only.

Any non-vertical line through this point has equation
$$y=mx+ap^2+(b-m)p+c.$$
Equating it with the parabola gives
$$\begin{align*}ax^2+bx+c&=mx+ap^2+(b-m)p+c\\ax^2+(b-m)x-ap^2-(b-m)p&=0.\end{align*}$$
A single intersection requires a repeated root:
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(b-m)^2+4a\bigl(ap^2+(b-m)p\bigr)\\\Delta&=(b-m+2ap)^2\\(b-m+2ap)^2&=0\\m&=2ap+b.\end{align*}$$
Substituting this slope gives
$$\begin{align*}y&=(2ap+b)x+ap^2-2ap^2+c\\y&=(2ap+b)x-ap^2+c.\end{align*}$$
Thus the two lines are $x=p$ and $y=(2ap+b)x-ap^2+c$.
